subject: Request: SLA exception for private deployment — latency & uptime
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@northpointhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: InfraOps Team <infraops@northpointhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA — region-specific carveouts request

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the deployment walkthrough yesterday. We ran this up the stack and Procurement + InfraOps have a couple of asks before we sign the private deployment contract: specifically around uptime and latency guarantees when the service is running on our VPC and via our network path to the GPU hosts.

Our ask is that the SLA language reflect a shared-responsibility carveout for network-layer incidents and scheduled maintenance on our side. Concretely: if packet loss or traffic-shaping on our transit route causes 5%+ request failures or p95 latency > 500ms for more than 30 minutes, we request that those windows be excluded from Redwood’s uptime calculation. We also want a clause that allows an agreed debugging window with our InfraOps (up to 4 hours) where remediation steps are collaborative and SLA credits are not issued until joint analysis is complete.

Attached are redlines (northpoint-sla-redlines.pdf) with suggested language. We can be flexible on thresholds but need protection for regulated workloads (PHI).

Can Redwood confirm acceptance in principle and any monitoring hooks you need from our side?

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Infrastructure — Northpoint Health

----
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@northpointhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — region-specific carveouts request

Alex —

Appreciate the clear redlines and context. Redwood is generally open to shared-responsibility carveouts for customer-managed networking and hardware. A few immediate notes:

- We can exclude customer-controlled network outages and any third-party transit incidents from our uptime calculation, provided there is mutual evidence (e.g., packet captures, traceroutes, or provider incident reports).
- For latency carveouts, we propose a p95 threshold of 400ms (rather than 500ms) for carveout eligibility; if p95 exceeds 400ms for more than 30 minutes and evidence points to customer-side network congestion, that window can be excluded.
- The joint debugging window you propose (up to 4 hours) is reasonable; for clarity we suggest the clause say: "Remediation window: up to 4 business hours for joint investigation following incident detection; credits are deferred until investigation completes and root cause is agreed."

To operationalize this we need: (1) a Prometheus scrape endpoint or metrics export from your side that shows request/response timings and error counts, (2) read-only access to VPC flow logs or a CloudEdge-provided transit report for the incident period, and (3) a primary InfraOps contact for on-call coordination.

Looping in Vivek and Laura to confirm contractual stance and any limits we should apply to multi-month credit deferral. I’ll put together revised contract text if we agree on the thresholds.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — region-specific carveouts request

Team,

High level: I support a shared-responsibility carveout but want guardrails so we don't create open-ended exclusions. Proposed contract guardrails:

- Max cumulative carveout per rolling 90-day period: 72 hours (unless mutually agreed emergency).
- For latency carveouts, require both (a) customer metrics showing elevated egress latency and (b) at least one corroborating transit-provider RCA or flow log showing packet drops/queueing.
- Limit debug-window deferral to a single 10-business-day period for each incident: credits are calculated after the investigation completes, but we will not defer acceptance indefinitely.

Also, for regulated customers handling PHI we should require encryption in transit (TLS 1.3) and an agreed SLA for incident notification (30 minutes). Put Legal on copy for final wording; Laura will lead.

Vivek
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

----
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — region-specific carveouts request

Vivek — noted. Legal will draft tight language around the 72-hour rolling cap, requirements for evidence, and limits on credit deferral. A couple of legal drafting points:

- Add a provision that Redwood may request a third-party network forensics report if there is disagreement on root cause — costs split unless malicious actions are suspected.
- Define "incident detection" to be when either party observes error rates above agreed thresholds or open support ticket with confirmed service-impacting events.

I’ll draft and share redlined contract text. Marcus, can you confirm whether a hosted fallback (Redwood-managed model variant in our hosted fleet) is feasible as a contractual fallback for critical PHI endpoints? If feasible we can offer a fallback route for a short failover window (30 minutes) to ensure continuity while the incident is being worked.

Laura
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference

----
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@northpointhealth.com>, InfraOps Team <infraops@northpointhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLA language and operational steps (attached)

Alex / InfraOps team —

Please find attached a proposed set of contract edits (PDF) and an integration checklist (Prometheus diagram attached). Summary of the operative items we agreed in principle on: 

1) Carveouts: Redwood will exclude customer-controlled network incidents from uptime calculations when (a) p95 latency >= 400ms for >= 30 minutes AND (b) evidence from customer metrics or transit-provider report corroborates customer-side impact.

2) Rolling cap: carveouts for network incidents will not exceed 72 cumulative hours in any rolling 90-day window unless both parties approve an exception.

3) Remediation window: joint investigation period up to 4 business hours for initial triage; final RCA allowed up to 10 business days for credit determination.

4) Monitoring hooks: Northpoint will provide a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint and one week of VPC flow logs for any disputed incident window.

5) Fallback: Redwood can provide a hosted fallback endpoint for up to 30 minutes during severe incidents for PHI routes; fallback activation requires written approval from Northpoint’s InfraOps. Charges for fallback use will be billed at the standard hosted rate.

Next steps: If you agree to the above, please sign the attached redline and return. Laura will produce final language for the contract.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Email: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0137

Attachment stubs: northpoint-sla-redlines.pdf (PDF), prometheus-integration-diagram.png (PNG)

----
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@northpointhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, InfraOps Team <infraops@northpointhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA language and operational steps (attached)

Stephanie —

Thanks, this looks acceptable in principle. Two small asks before we sign: (1) move the p95 threshold to 425ms (we can live with 400ms but prefer 425ms as a middle ground) and (2) confirm the fallback activation process: can InfraOps trigger fallback via email + a short webhook to your incident API? If both are ok we’ll get Procurement on the signature path.

I’ll mark up the PDF and return.

Alex
Director, Infrastructure — Northpoint Health
